items.text: Our approach
Not every asking price *reflects the market*
The price a home is advertised at isn't necessarily the value it can sell for.

Not all advertised homes are truly comparable, and not every published price reflects market value. That's why we study what's on offer, the references from completed sales, where reliable information is available, and the particulars of each property.
Illustrative diagram, no real data.
What our valuation includes
Four analyses, *one well-reasoned valuation*
A valuation with an advisor goes through these four steps. When we hand it over, we explain what we studied in each one and how we reached the conclusion.
Your home
We look at its surface area, layout, condition, orientation, natural light, construction features and anything else that can affect its value.
Surface areas and measurements
Condition
Cadastral data and planning information
Available documents
Its location
We analyse the neighbourhood, its surroundings and the features of the local property market.
Location and surroundings
Neighbourhood profile
Market trends
The real market
We pick comparable properties, study the competition currently on the market and cross-check the information with the sales references available.
Comparable homes
Properties currently advertised
Sales references, when available
Our valuation
We interpret what we've gathered to reach a well-reasoned estimate of market value and, if you want to sell, to recommend how to position your home.
Market value estimate
Commercial positioning
Asking price, where relevant

Frequently asked questions
What people usually ask us

items.q: What's the difference between an online valuation and a professional one?
items.a: The online valuation gives you an indicative estimate instantly, based on the details you enter. The valuation with an advisor studies your home individually — its condition, its documents and its market — and explains which factors affect its value. We go into more detail in the article [Is the online valuation of your flat reliable?](route:blog)

items.q: How is the market value of a home determined?
items.a: By analysing the property's features, its location and the market: comparable homes, advertised supply and sales references where available. The result is a reasoned estimate, not a guaranteed sale price.

items.q: Is a property valuation the same as an official appraisal?
items.a: No. An official appraisal is carried out by an accredited appraisal company and is usually requested by the bank for a mortgage. Our valuation is a market study to guide your decisions.

items.q: Can I ask for a valuation even if I haven't decided to sell?
items.a: Yes. Many owners ask for one to decide whether to sell and when. It's also useful with an inheritance, a divorce or a split between co-owners, or simply to know the value of your assets.

items.q: What happens after I request a valuation?
items.a: With the online valuation you get the estimate instantly. If you ask for one with an advisor, we call you to arrange the visit and follow the four steps above. If you then decide to sell, the valuation is the starting point of our [sales brokerage](service:venta-estrategica) service.
